gen-gf-autour-one-gf-ubuntu-sans: Round, loud letters with a smooth runway into every curve. Autour One does the shouting while Ubuntu Sans, with its big-eyed lowercase and pipe-like strokes, stays quietly modern underneath.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-armata: Tall, bold lowercase that nearly stands as high as its capitals. Gugi holds full-width stroke joins where Armata, the sans-serif body, leaves spacious gaps between characters, and that difference is the pair.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-liter: Tall lowercase, cut-open terminals, and a bold stance. Liter draws with no stroke contrast and wide mouths on its rounds, giving the Gugi heading a quiet place to land.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-miriam-libre: Tall, bold lowercase with cut-open terminals. Gugi does best at bold, flowing counters with curves that match its stems, while Miriam Libre does best at approachable, wire-weight sans-serif lines.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-mochiy-pop-p-one: Tall, bold lowercase with terminals cut open. Gugi earns its keep big and brief, while Mochiy Pop P One lays a wide stretch of blank space between letters in clean sans-serif style.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-brahmi: Tall, cut-open lowercase with a bold, distinctive look. Noto Sans Brahmi keeps a high mean line and open-ended curves, so extended reading should feel light and unhurried beside Gugi.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Noto Sans Tai Le reads gently, with tapering ink strokes. Pages of it stay approachable, and the Gugi heading, cut to a single depth, gives the eye a bold place to start.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-ugaritic: Tall, bold lowercase with terminals cut open. Noto Sans Ugaritic does best at approachable, clean sans text with open mouths like unjoined chalk arcs, while Gugi does best at bold headings.
gen-gf-goldman-gf-stack-sans-text: Goldman sets wide, commanding letters with generous clearance. Stack Sans Text draws a marker-like constant line with well-separated curve endings, so its plain sans text moves along without friction.
gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-gf-noto-san: Noto Sans Mono sets generously spaced, tall-lowercase sans-serif letters that never bump together, with openings in every curve. Love Ya Like A Sister earns its keep big and short.
